title: A unit differential entry splits off an identity complex
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $C_\bullet$ be a chain complex of finite free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with differential $d_i:C_i\to C_{i-1}$ and $d_{i-1}d_i=0$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$. If some matrix coefficient of one $d_i$ in finite bases of $C_i$ and $C_{i-1}$ is a unit, then $C_\bullet$ is isomorphic as a chain complex to $C'_\bullet\oplus T_\bullet$, where every $C'_j$ is finite free, $C'_i$ and $C'_{i-1}$ have ranks one less than $C_i$ and $C_{i-1}$ respectively, $C'_j$ has the same rank as $C_j$ for every other $j$, and $T_\bullet$ is zero outside degrees $i$ and $i-1$ and is $R\xrightarrow{1}R$ in those two degrees. Here $C'_\bullet\oplus T_\bullet$ is the complex with terms the direct sums $C'_j\oplus T_j$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] and differential $d'_j\oplus d^T_j$, and an isomorphism of chain complexes is a family of $R$-linear bijections $\psi_j:C'_j\oplus T_j\to C_j$ with $d_j\psi_j=\psi_{j-1}(d'_j\oplus d^T_j)$ for all $j$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MT (lemma-add-trivial-complex, line 24608), statement and proof, lines 24608--24650

proof.text: (Normalising the unit entry.) Write $n_j$ for the rank of $C_j$. Choose the finite bases $e_1,\dots,e_{n_i}$ of $C_i$ and $g_1,\dots,g_{n_{i-1}}$ of $C_{i-1}$ in which a coefficient of $d_i$ is a unit, and write $d_i(e_j)=\sum_k a_{jk}g_k$. Renumbering both bases we may assume that $u=a_{11}$ is the unit coefficient (so $n_i,n_{i-1}\ge1$). Put $f_1=d_i(e_1)=\sum_k a_{1k}g_k$ and $f_k=g_k$ for $2\le k\le n_{i-1}$. The coefficient matrix of $(f_k)$ in the basis $(g_k)$ has first row $(a_{11},a_{12},\dots)$ and $k$-th row the $k$-th unit row for $k\ge2$: it vanishes below the diagonal and its diagonal entries $a_{11},1,\dots,1$ are units. By [lem-weil-pbc-triangular-change-of-basis], $f_1,\dots,f_{n_{i-1}}$ is a basis of $C_{i-1}$, and $d_i(e_1)=f_1$. This is the source's 'after a change of basis of $R^{n_i}$ and $R^{n_{i-1}}$ the first basis vector of $R^{n_i}$ is mapped to the first basis vector of $R^{n_{i-1}}$'.

(Clearing the first column.) Write $d_i(e_j)=\sum_k b_{jk}f_k$ in the new basis of $C_{i-1}$; by Step 1, $b_{11}=1$ and $b_{1k}=0$ for $k\ge2$. Put $e'_1=e_1$ and $e'_j=e_j-b_{j1}e_1$ for $2\le j\le n_i$. The coefficient matrix of $(e'_j)$ in the basis $(e_j)$ has $-b_{j1}$ in position $(j,1)$ for $j\ge2$, $1$ on the diagonal and $0$ elsewhere, so it vanishes above the diagonal with unit diagonal, and by [lem-weil-pbc-triangular-change-of-basis] $e'_1,\dots,e'_{n_i}$ is a basis of $C_i$. By linearity $d_i(e'_j)=d_i(e_j)-b_{j1}f_1=\sum_{k\ge2}b_{jk}f_k$ for $j\ge2$: in the new bases the coefficient of $f_1$ in $d_i(e'_j)$ vanishes for $j>1$ (the source's '$a_{j1}=0$ for $j>1$').

(The two decompositions.) Let $C'_i\subset C_i$ be the submodule spanned by $e'_2,\dots,e'_{n_i}$ and $C'_{i-1}\subset C_{i-1}$ the submodule spanned by $f_2,\dots,f_{n_{i-1}}$. Since $(e'_j)$ and $(f_k)$ are bases, every $x\in C_i$ is uniquely $x=r e'_1+y$ with $r\in R$, $y\in C'_i$, and every $z\in C_{i-1}$ is uniquely $z=s f_1+w$ with $s\in R$, $w\in C'_{i-1}$; $e'_2,\dots,e'_{n_i}$ is a basis of $C'_i$ and $f_2,\dots,f_{n_{i-1}}$ a basis of $C'_{i-1}$ (a subfamily of a basis is a basis of its span), so $C'_i$, $C'_{i-1}$ are free of ranks $n_i-1$, $n_{i-1}-1$. By Steps 1 and 2, $d_i(e'_1)=f_1$ and $d_i(C'_i)\subset C'_{i-1}$.

(The incoming differential avoids $e'_1$.) Let $x\in C_{i+1}$ and write $d_{i+1}(x)=r e'_1+y$ as in Step 3. Then $0=d_id_{i+1}(x)=r f_1+d_i(y)$ with $d_i(y)\in C'_{i-1}$; by uniqueness of the decomposition of $C_{i-1}$ in Step 3, $r=0$. Hence $d_{i+1}(C_{i+1})\subset C'_i$ (the source's 'the image of $R^{n_{i+1}}\to R^{n_i}$ is contained in the subspace spanned by $e_j$, $j>1$').
(The outgoing differential kills $f_1$.) $d_{i-1}(f_1)=d_{i-1}d_i(e'_1)=0$ (the source's '$R^{n_{i-1}}\to R^{n_{i-2}}$ has to annihilate $f_1$ since it is in the image').

(Assembling the splitting.) Define $C'_ ullet$ by $C'_j=C_j$ for $j
otin\{i,i-1\}$ and $C'_i$, $C'_{i-1}$ as in Step 3, with differentials $d'_j=d_j$ for $j
otin\{i+1,i,i-1\}$, $d'_{i+1}=d_{i+1}:C_{i+1}	o C'_i$ (allowed by Step 4), $d'_i=d_i|_{C'_i}:C'_i	o C'_{i-1}$ (Step 3) and $d'_{i-1}=d_{i-1}|_{C'_{i-1}}:C'_{i-1}	o C_{i-2}$; each $d'_{j-1}d'_j$ is a restriction of $d_{j-1}d_j=0$, so $C'_ ullet$ is a chain complex of finite free modules with the stated ranks (Step 3). Let $T_ ullet$ be $R\xrightarrow{1}R$ in degrees $i,i-1$ and $0$ elsewhere, and $C'_ ullet\oplus T_ ullet$ the degreewise direct sum [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] with differential $d'_j\oplus d^T_j$. Define $\psi_j:C'_j\oplus T_j	o C_j$ by $\psi_j(y,t)=y$ for $j
otin\{i,i-1\}$, $\psi_i(y,r)=y+re'_1$ and $\psi_{i-1}(w,s)=w+sf_1$; each $\psi_j$ is $R$-linear and bijective (Step 3). Compatibility $d_j\psi_j=\psi_{j-1}(d'_j\oplus d^T_j)$: in degree $i+1$ both sides send $x$ to $d_{i+1}x$ (Step 4, $T_i$-component $0$); in degree $i$, $d_i(y+re'_1)=d_i(y)+rf_1=\psi_{i-1}(d_iy,r)$ (Step 3); in degree $i-1$, $d_{i-1}(w+sf_1)=d_{i-1}(w)$ by Step 5, which is $\psi_{i-2}(d'_{i-1}w,0)$; in every other degree both sides are $d_j$. So $\psi$ is an isomorphism of chain complexes $C'_ ullet\oplus T_ ullet\cong C_ ullet$ (the source's 'these conditions and the shape of the matrix imply the lemma').

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 00MT line by line. The source's proof cites no lemma; its two changes of basis (normalising the unit entry to 1, clearing the column of $e_1$) are used without proof that the new families are bases, so that fact is the new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-triangular-change-of-basis (triangular coefficient matrix with unit diagonal gives a basis; Mathlib has it only through Basis.is_basis_iff_det plus triangular determinants, recorded as candidate). The remaining steps (decomposition into spans of subfamilies, image of d_{i+1} avoids e_1 since d_i d_{i+1}=0, d_{i-1}(f_1)=0, and the explicit isomorphism with C' + T, which the source leaves as 'these conditions ... imply the lemma') are written out and are elementary given the definitions. The statement was kept and made self-contained: the direct sum of complexes and the isomorphism of chain complexes are now spelled out, with def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules added to stmt_deps. Item Mathlib searches redone in the SETUP checkout (the old grep was of another machine's checkout and was replaced); no match. No slopmaster2 Lean found (grep by id, tag 00MT and key words).

lean.statement: theorem exists_splitting_of_isUnit_entry {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (C : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ) (n : ℤ → ℕ) (b : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Basis (Fin (n j)) R (C.X j)) (i : ℤ) (p : Fin (n i)) (q : Fin (n (i - 1))) (hunit : IsUnit (LinearMap.toMatrix (b i) (b (i - 1)) (C.d i (i - 1)).hom q p)) : ∃ (C' T : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ) (n' : ℤ → ℕ), (∀ j : ℤ, Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin (n' j)) R (C'.X j))) ∧ n' i + 1 = n i ∧ n' (i - 1) + 1 = n (i - 1) ∧ (∀ j : ℤ, j ≠ i → j ≠ i - 1 → n' j = n j) ∧ (∀ j : ℤ, j ≠ i → j ≠ i - 1 → Subsingleton (T.X j)) ∧ ∃ (e : T.X i ≃ₗ[R] R) (f : T.X (i - 1) ≃ₗ[R] R), (∀ t : T.X i, f ((T.d i (i - 1)).hom t) = e t) ∧ let M : ℤ → Bool → ModuleCat.{max u v} R := fun j s ↦ if s then T.X j else C'.X j ∃ ψ : ∀ j : ℤ, (⨁ s : Bool, M j s) ≃ₗ[R] C.X j, ∀ (j : ℤ) (x : C'.X j) (t : T.X j), (C.d j (j - 1)).hom (ψ j (DirectSum.lof R Bool (fun s ↦ M j s) false x + DirectSum.lof R Bool (fun s ↦ M j s) true t)) = ψ (j - 1) (DirectSum.lof R Bool (fun s ↦ M (j - 1) s) false ((C'.d j (j - 1)).hom x) + DirectSum.lof R Bool (fun s ↦ M (j - 1) s) true ((T.d j (j - 1)).hom t))
